front: Which deer is which? Name the clues.
back: Left: mule deer. Forked antlers, big ears, thin white tail with a black tip, big white rump. Right: white tailed deer. One main beam with single tines, wide brown tail flagged white when alarmed.

front: A deer bounces away on all 4 feet at once. Which species?
back: Mule deer. The bounce is called stotting. White tails gallop with the tail up.

front: Name the 4 ducks by shape and flight.
back: Mallard: big, slow wingbeats. Green winged teal: small, very fast, flock twists. Wigeon: white wing patch, whistles. Goldeneye: a diver, wings set far back, wings whistle.

front: Puddle duck or diver: how do they take off?
back: Puddle ducks (mallard, teal, wigeon) jump straight up. Divers (goldeneye, bufflehead, scaup) run along the water to get airborne.

front: Deer track: which way did it walk, and what are the 2 small dots behind it?
back: The pointed tips point the way it walked. The 2 dots are dewclaws, which show in soft mud, snow or when running.

front: A twig is bitten off. Clean 45 degree cut, or ragged and torn. Who ate it?
back: Clean angled cut: hare or rabbit (they have upper incisors). Ragged, torn tip: deer, moose or elk (no upper front teeth, they tear).

front: Morning on a sunny slope. Which way does your scent go, and where should you be?
back: Warming air rises uphill. Be above the deer in the morning, below them in the evening when cooling air sinks.
